events.title: Mayflower Departs Plymouth, Massachusetts
events.description: After wintering in the New World, the Mayflower left Plymouth on its return voyage to England, leaving the Pilgrim settlers behind to build their colony. The ship had carried the settlers across the Atlantic in 1620 and lost roughly half its crew over the winter.
events.significance: The settlers' decision to stay and the ship's departure marked the commitment of the Plymouth Colony to permanent settlement, a foundational episode in the early English colonization of North America.

events.title: Anne Sullivan Begins Teaching Helen Keller
events.description: Anne Sullivan arrived at the Keller home in Tuscumbia, Alabama, in March 1887, and on April 5 she achieved a breakthrough when Helen Keller, who was deaf and blind, understood that the finger-spelled word 'water' referred to the water flowing over her hand.
events.significance: This moment of language comprehension transformed Keller's life, enabling her to become an author, activist, and lecturer, and it influenced education for people with disabilities worldwide.

events.title: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg Sentenced to Death
events.description: A US federal judge sentenced Julius and Ethel Rosenberg to death after they were convicted of conspiracy to commit espionage for passing atomic secrets to the Soviet Union.
events.significance: The case became a defining event of the early Cold War and McCarthy era, provoking decades of debate about espionage, anti-communist fervor, and the fairness of the trial. The Rosenbergs were executed in 1953.

events.title: Death of Kurt Cobain
events.description: Kurt Cobain, lead singer and guitarist of the grunge band Nirvana, died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound at his home in Seattle. His body was found on April 8, and the date of death is estimated as April 5.
events.significance: Cobain's death at age 27 marked the loss of a defining voice of Generation X and the alternative rock movement, and it sparked wider conversations about mental health, addiction, and fame.

events.title: Battle of Maipú
events.description: Chilean and Argentine forces under José de San Martín decisively defeated Spanish royalist troops at the Battle of Maipú near Santiago, Chile.
events.significance: The victory secured Chile's independence from Spain and was a major step in the South American wars of independence, opening the way for the liberation of Peru.
